introduction: Tailored for JEE Advanced and complex conceptual questions in NEET, this level covers capillarity mechanics, efflux dynamics from holes, Reynolds numbers, and elastic energy density analytics.

core_concepts.title: Torricelli's Law of Efflux
core_concepts.description: The speed at which a liquid flows out of an orifice (small hole) at a depth $h$ below the open surface of a tank is identical to the speed a free-falling body acquires jumping from the same height: $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.

core_concepts.title: Capillary Rise (Jurin's Law)
core_concepts.description: The rise or fall of a liquid inside a narrow tube of radius $r$ dipped into it. The height achieved is $h = (2T \cos\theta)/(\rho gr)$, where $\theta$ is the Angle of Contact between the liquid and the tube wall.

core_concepts.title: Reynolds Number ($R_e$)
core_concepts.description: A pure dimensionless parameter that predicts whether a fluid flow will be laminar (smooth) or turbulent (chaotic). Given by $R_e = (\rho v D)/\eta$. If $R_e < 1000$, the flow is steady and laminar.

core_concepts.title: Elastic Energy Density
core_concepts.description: The potential energy stored per unit volume in a stretched elastic solid: $U/V = 0.5 \times \text{Stress} \times \text{Strain} = 0.5 \times Y \times (\text{Strain})^2$.

important_entities.name: Vena Contracta
important_entities.key_fact: The point of minimum cross-sectional area in an efflux stream.
important_entities.significance: Located just outside the orifice. It is the precise location where the liquid jet streamlines become parallel, making it the mathematically correct zone to apply Bernoulli's equation.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Obtuse Contact Angles and Capillary Depression
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If the contact angle $\theta > 90^\circ$ (obtuse), as seen between mercury and glass, the term $\cos\theta$ becomes negative. The fluid level drops ($h$ is negative) instead of rising, creating a convex meniscus.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If a large tank of area $A$ is filled to height $H$ and leaks through a tiny base hole of area $a$, the absolute time required to empty the entire tank completely can be computed directly using this calculus derivation shorthand.

exam_strategy_tips: In JEE Advanced questions where a capillary setup is placed inside an accelerating elevator or satellite, replace $g$ with the effective gravity vector ($g_{\text{eff}}$). In zero gravity ($g=0$), the liquid will completely fill the tube up to the very top, regardless of its length.
